planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in shade to partial shade; the outsized leaves of Giganteum make a bold, tropical-looking statement in a shaded bed or large container.

directions: Plant in consistently moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in shade to partial shade, sheltered from harsh sun that scorches the leaves. Giganteum is a large-scale variety of Farfugium japonicum, the Gulf Coast garden staple known as leopard plant, producing rounded, glossy, deep-green leaves considerably larger than the straight species — often close to a foot across on mature plants — giving it a bold, almost tropical presence in a shade bed. Clusters of small, daisy-like yellow flowers rise above the foliage on tall stems in fall. Its large scale makes it a strong focal point or specimen plant rather than a filler, and like other farfugium it tolerates deep shade and dense root competition under trees better than most broadleaf perennials.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in constantly moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; like all ligularia, Othello wilts dramatically in afternoon sun or dry soil, so site it in a reliably damp, sheltered spot.

directions: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in constantly moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; site it in reliably damp ground, since plants scorch and wilt badly in anything less regardless of shade level. Othello is a classic Ligularia dentata cultivar, its large, rounded leaves tinted purple-bronze on top with a deep mahogany-purple underside, topped in mid to late summer by tall clusters of vivid orange-yellow, daisy-like flowers that contrast strongly with the dark foliage. It has been a garden standard for its combination of bold dark leaves and bright late-summer bloom, making a dramatic accent at a pond edge, rain garden, or the moist, shaded portion of a mixed border. Slugs can be a persistent problem on the tender young growth in consistently damp settings; handpick or use organic slug controls as needed.

common_name: King's Ransom Brunnera (Deep Silver Green-Veined Siberian Bugloss)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; holds its silver leaf color best out of hot afternoon sun.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to deep shade, keeping soil evenly moist through summer since foliage can wilt or scorch in dry conditions or hot sun. King's Ransom bears bold, heart-shaped leaves densely covered in shimmering silver, traced by a fine network of contrasting dark green veins that stand out sharply against the pale background, topped by airy sprays of small, bright blue, forget-me-not-like flowers in early spring. Its densely silvered foliage lights up shaded corners from spring through fall, long after the modest spring flowers have finished, and pairs beautifully with hostas, ferns, and hellebores in a woodland border. Established clumps rarely need division and self-seed only sparingly compared to the plain species.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade. Moonshine produces leaves almost entirely covered in bright, luminous silver with only a thin green edge, one of the most heavily silvered lungwort cultivars available, glowing in dim shade in a way few other foliage plants can match. Clusters of small, funnel-shaped flowers open pink and mature to blue in early spring, appearing before many companion shade perennials leaf out and providing an early nectar source for emerging bumblebees. Its bright, near-white foliage effect makes it a strong accent for lighting up dark corners; divide congested clumps in early fall every few years to maintain vigor.

common_name: Blue Ensign Pulmonaria (Solid Green Vivid Blue-Flowered Lungwort)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade. Blue Ensign is an Award of Garden Merit-winning lungwort valued for its unusually vivid, deep cobalt-blue flowers, among the most intensely colored of any pulmonaria cultivar, held above plain, unspotted green leaves rather than the silver-mottled foliage typical of most lungwort cultivars. Its early spring bloom, opening before many companion shade perennials leaf out, provides an important nectar source for emerging bumblebees, and its solid green leaves offer a plainer foliage backdrop that lets the striking blue flowers stand out. Divide congested clumps in early fall every few years to maintain vigor and flowering.

common_name: Milky Way Cast Iron Plant (White-Speckled Deep-Shade Aspidistra)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral soil in partial to deep shade. Milky Way is a striking selection of the legendary cast iron plant, its broad, strap-shaped, leathery evergreen leaves densely dusted with small white speckles across the entire leaf surface, a starry, luminous pattern distinct from the bolder longitudinal stripes of other variegated aspidistra cultivars. Like the species, it tolerates the deepest, driest shade of nearly any ornamental perennial, thriving in the difficult dark, root-filled ground under mature live oaks and other dense-canopy trees where few other plants survive. It is essentially maintenance-free once established, extremely drought-tolerant, deer-resistant, and slow-growing enough that division is rarely needed except to propagate new plantings.

common_name: Okame Cast Iron Plant (Broad White-Striped Aspidistra)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral soil in partial to deep shade. Okame is a classic Japanese cast iron plant selection with broad, bold, creamy-white longitudinal stripes running the length of each leathery, strap-shaped leaf, a strong, high-contrast variegation pattern that brightens the darkest corners of a shade garden. Like the species, it tolerates extraordinary neglect — drought, poor light, root competition from trees, and long stretches without care — making it a cornerstone of low-maintenance Gulf South shade gardening under live oaks and other dense-canopy trees. It is slow-growing, deer-resistant, and essentially maintenance-free once established; division is rarely needed except to propagate new plants.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown specimens in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral, average to humus-rich soil in partial to full shade in spring; variegation is best appreciated with some indirect light rather than the deepest shade.

directions: Plant divisions in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral, average to humus-rich soil in partial to full shade. Nishiki is a variegated selection of rohdea (sacred lily, omoto), a Japanese collector's plant with a centuries-long cultivation history, bearing glossy, dark-green, strap-shaped leaves marked with irregular cream-to-yellow striping that gives the clump a jeweled, patterned appearance distinct from the solid-green species. Like the plain species, it tolerates extreme shade and dry, root-filled soil under mature trees that defeats most other evergreen perennials, and inconspicuous spring flowers are followed by bright red berries in fall. Extremely long-lived, drought-tolerant once established, deer-resistant, and essentially maintenance-free; berries are toxic if ingested.
